newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares rebound in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares rebound in active trading.

text.p: Shanghai B shares reversed early losses late in the session due to bargain-hunting and overcame a fall in market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development because of the poor performance of its warrants, brokers said.
The index rose 0.575 points or 1.24 percent to 46.775 points, on volume of 22.6 million shares worth $4.4 million, of which trading of Lujiazui's warrants accounted for 12.0 million shares.
Of 41 B shares, 36 traded, with 19 up, eight flat and nine down.
Brokers said institutions started buying over-sold stocks late in the session, which sparked follow-up buying and pushed the index up.

"Institutions seemed to ignore falls in Lujiazui and began to build positions in selected stocks, which give some confidence to the market," one broker said. "Overseas liquidation selling was seen fading with prices so low, which supported the index."
Shanghai Lujiazui fell $0.012 or 10.71 percent to $0.124, on volume of 20,000 shares, with its warrant's price $0.038.
"Trading volume increased in the afternoon with the index rising, which improved the technical charts, and further rises are likely," a second broker said.
Shanghai Jintai was the star on a technical rebound, jumping $0.012 or 10.71 percent to $0.124, on volume of 20,000 shares.

Shanghai Posts & Communication Equipment traded the most on institutional bargain-hunting after sharp losses in the past few weeks, brokers said. It rose $0.008 or 2.96 percent to $0.278 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Shanghai A share index rose on active speculation in selective stocks, brokers said.

The index gained 13.358 points or 1.35 percent to 1003.437 points on volume of 476.6 million shares worth 4.4 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 20.660 points or 0.84 percent to 2475.226 points.
Speculative stock Shanghai ACE Electronics was the star, soaring 1.58 yuan or 12.98 percent to 13.75 yuan, on volume of 20. 5 million shares.
